x: Joe McDonald (42yrs) and Charlie Smart (55yrs) had a personal battle in this race. Charlie led down the hills and Joe up them, but the "youngster" had that final edge and, what's more, took the Veterans prize also!

Jack Brown and Mike Shingles also ran well to finish 7th and 10th respectively,but we still only managed 2nd team behind Maidstone who packed 3,4 and 5. Outside the scoring three were the "Duke's Joggers",namely Gordon Biscoe,Joe McDonald,Derek Crookes and Charlie Smart.
JOE McDONALD

However, our final trio of Bill Lucas (receiving the full backing of the cross-country team!) Joe McDonald and our former Empire Champion, Arthur Penny, were no match for the strong finish of our hosts and we went down by 1½ laps.

Ray Beaumont was a deserved second and that popular "vet" Joe McDonald third. Joe was delighted at being amongst the prizes and also at beating his training companion, the evergreen Charlie Smart; though he would probably agree that their handicap allowances should have been reversed on pre-race form.

Of late he can be seen regularly in the company of that other "character" and veteran, Joe McDonald. Thanks to each other they are both running better than for some time and Mac will be the first to vouch for the remarkable ability of his 60 years old companion.

In the kaleidoscope one recalls Bob Glover smiling, Joe McDonald commenting, "∂*! good do en it. No, I mean it's really *[illegible] good, everything's [illegible]** good!" with such honesty that it was a joy to hear him.
Someone like Pete Sutton who sweeps out the canteen and committee room, someone like Joe McDonald who at the hint of a suggestion is so eager to please, or Fred Paget washing up and running a bar.
A special mention must be made for Joe McDonald. Running in his second vets race within a month he improved by an astonishing 3½ minutes over the same 5 mile course.

Colin Pearson upset Pat O'Connor against the odds and Brian Gorman ('Don't put me in the relay team') had a remarkable run; but for most, onlookers and runners alike, the man of the race was Joe McDonald.

Our model Joseph McDonald displays what the better dressed runner was wearing around 1951 - a charming ensemble of claret short sleeved jersey, hooped in gold with cross keys and portcullis motif over the heart, matched with a delightful pair of slinky 'off the knee' white cotton shorts.

In the over 50 event 2nd claim member Jack Brown (Cambridge H) was the winner in 36:13. The Belgrave team scored 61pts for 7th place with E.Young 23rd in 41:23, Joe McDonald 31st in 42:26 and John Baker 44th in 43:47.
But just look who took second, none other than Joe McDonald, showing disdain for his increased handicap penalty after recent successes by revealing even more speed than normal.
